item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
A rectangular garden that is next to a building has a path around the other three sides, as shown.

[Image: Diagram of a garden and path next to a building]

What is the area of the path?
item.figure_description: A diagram shows a thick line labeled "Building" forming a vertical wall. Directly adjacent to the building wall is a shaded rectangular "Garden", surrounded on the remaining three sides by an unshaded "Path" forming a larger outer rectangle. The dimensions shown are: total vertical height of the outer rectangle along the building wall is 12 m; horizontal length of the garden is 10 m; vertical height of the garden is 8 m; and total horizontal width of the outer rectangle (garden plus path width) along the bottom is 12 m.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Shaded rectangular diagram that is x meters by x plus 4 meters. A white, width-wise rectangular path goes down the middle of the diagram and is 1 meter by x meters.]

This is a diagram of a rectangular garden.

The white area is a rectangular path that is 1 meter wide.

Which expression shows the area of the shaded portion of the garden in m^2?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle with height labeled x m and total width labeled (x + 4) m. The rectangle is divided vertically into three sections: a shaded gray rectangular region on the left, a vertical white rectangular strip labeled "path" in the middle, and another shaded gray rectangular region on the right. An arrow beneath the white path indicates its width is 1 m.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A rectangular shaped swimming pool has a paved walkway around it as shown.

[Image: Diagram of a pool and walkway]

What is the area of the paved walkway?
reference_items.figure_description: A diagram shows an outer shaded rectangle labeled "Walkway" surrounding an unshaded inner rectangle labeled "Pool". The dimensions of the outer rectangle are labeled with double-headed arrows: a length of 70 m along the top and a width of 23 m along the right side. The dimensions of the inner rectangle are also labeled with double-headed arrows: a length of 50 m along its top edge and a width of 18 m along its right edge.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A rectangle, with one side x and the other side, x plus 2.]

What is the area of this rectangle?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle is shown with dimension lines. The horizontal bottom side is indicated by a dimension line with tick marks at both ends and labeled x + 2. The vertical right side is indicated by a dimension line with tick marks at both ends and labeled x.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A shaded rectangle that is 6 cm by 16 cm. Part of the rectangle is unshaded. The unshaded part of the rectangle forms a right triangle on the left that is 6 centimeters by 8 centimeters.]

In the figure above, what is the area of the shaded region in cm^2?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle with a height of 6 cm and a total length of 16 cm along the top, both labeled with dimension arrows. An unshaded right triangle occupies the bottom-left portion of the rectangle; its vertical leg is the left side of the rectangle (6 cm) and its horizontal leg along the bottom has a length of 8 cm labeled with a dimension arrow. The remainder of the rectangle is shaded solid black.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: L-shaped polygon]

What is the area, in square cm, of the figure shown above?
reference_items.figure_description: An L-shaped polygon with six sides. The leftmost vertical side is labeled 8 cm. The bottom horizontal side is labeled 12 cm. From the top-left vertex, a horizontal top edge extends to the right to meet a vertical segment that goes downward, labeled 3 cm. From the bottom of that 3 cm segment, a horizontal edge labeled 9 cm extends to the right to meet the rightmost vertical side. Right-angle symbols are marked at five vertices: the top-left vertex, the vertex where the top horizontal edge meets the 3 cm vertical segment, the vertex where the 9 cm segment meets the right vertical side, the bottom-right vertex, and the bottom-left vertex.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which of these could represent the expression 2x + 3x?

options.label: A
options.text: The length of this segment: [Image: X and 5 are segment lengths on a number line, and the segment length of 5 is slightly larger than the segment length of x.]

options.label: B
options.text: The length of this segment: [Image: 2, 3, and x are segment lengths on a number line. The segment length of 2 is the smallest. The segment length of 3 is around twice the length of 2, and the segment length of x is almost three times the length of 2.]

options.label: C
options.text: The area of this figure: [Image: A rectangle, where one side of the rectangle is labeled “x” and the other side is divided, with the smaller part labeled 2, and the larger part other labeled 3.]

options.label: D
options.text: The area of this figure: [Image: A rectangle, with one side is labeled 5 and the other side is divided in two equal parts, with each part labeled with “x”.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four options showing visual representations:
- Option A shows a horizontal line segment with vertical tick marks at its ends, divided into two segments by an interior vertical tick mark. The segment on the left is labeled x above, and the segment on the right is labeled 5 above.
- Option B shows a horizontal line segment with vertical tick marks at its ends, divided into three segments by two interior vertical tick marks. From left to right, the segments are labeled 2, 3, and x above.
- Option C shows a rectangle with its left vertical side labeled x. A vertical dotted line extends through the rectangle, dividing the top horizontal side into two parts, labeled 2 on the left and 3 on the right.
- Option D shows a rectangle with its left vertical side labeled 5. A vertical dotted line extends through the rectangle, dividing the top horizontal side into two equal parts, each labeled x above.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Front of a building with a car parked outside]

The car is 3.5 m long. About how long is the building?
reference_items.figure_description: A line drawing showing the front facade of a single-story building. In the center is a double door with an arched window above it. Symmetrically flanking the doors are six identical rectangular windows with multipaned sashes: three windows to the left of the door and three to the right. Parked on the ground along the far left of the building facade is a black car, positioned spanning the space of roughly the first two windows. The length of the entire building is approximately four times the length of the car.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
This table shows temperatures at various times on four days.

| TEMPERATURE | | | | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| | 6 a.m. | 9 a.m. | Noon | 3 p.m. | 6 p.m. |
| Monday | 15° | 17° | 24° | 21° | 16° |
| Tuesday | 20° | 16° | 15° | 10° | 9° |
| Wednesday | 8° | 14° | 16° | 19° | 15° |
| Thursday | 8° | 11° | 19° | 26° | 20° |

[Image: Thermometer]

On which day and at what time was the temperature shown in the table the same as that shown on the thermometer?
reference_items.figure_description: A vertical thermometer labeled "Thermometer" at the bottom. The scale on the right has labeled marks at 5°, 10°, 15°, 20°, 25°, 30°, 35°, and 40°, with individual 1-degree tick marks between them. The shaded column of liquid inside the thermometer reaches exactly 24° (one tick mark below 25°).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Rectangle ABCD containing two tangent circles P and Q]

In the figure above, ABCD is a rectangle, and circles P and Q each have a radius of 5 cm. What is the area of the rectangle?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle ABCD is oriented horizontally with vertices labeled A at the top-left, B at the top-right, C at the bottom-right, and D at the bottom-left. Inside the rectangle are two identical circles labeled P and Q, with their centers marked by dots labeled P and Q. The two circles are tangent to each other horizontally at the midline of the rectangle. Circle P touches the left side AD, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. Circle Q touches circle P, the right side BC, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. A vertical line segment is drawn from center P up to the point of tangency on top side AB, labeled "5 cm".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
